 Yaxel Lendeborg opens up on the transition to NBA amid Warriors struggles 
 2026-10-25 20:23 
 Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg is adjusting to the fast-paced NBA schedule after a 0-3 start. While averaging 18.7 points and 8.3 rebounds, the forward earned praise from Steve Kerr for his offensive versatility, though Kerr emphasized a need for better defensive awareness.
 Credit: Getty Images via AFP - Scanpix 
 Credit Getty Images via AFP - Scanpix

 Despite the Golden State Warriors starting their season with three consecutive losses, rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has looked like a solid NBA player from the start.

 Lendeborg spoke to Phoenix Suns reporter Duane Rankin about his transition to the NBA from college and how different losing in the league feels after a defeat against the Suns.
 "It’s tough in the NBA to win, you know. It’s like, in college, you’ll dwell over the loss for a little while. Like, right now, I’m very defeated," he said.
 "I feel like we can’t buy a win for nothing, but we have a game in two days. So I just got to try to flush it out of my system. Maybe dwell for an hour or so and just worry about the next. So, I mean, that’s something I definitely have to get adjusted with, and just figuring out ways to be effective everywhere else."
 Lendeborg still needs to adjust to NBA defenses
 Steve Kerr Yaxel Lendeborg Credit AP - Scanpix Following the loss to the Suns, head coach Steve Kerr pointed out Lendeborg's offensive skillset, but said that the forward still needs to improve on defense.
 "He's fearless. He's huge, and he's got a great skill set. He can dribble, pass, and shoot," Kerr said.
 "The defensive side is where I want to see the most improvement. His weak-side awareness right now is very poor."
 The 24-year-old forward shot 9-of-19 from the field and knocked down six of his 11 three-point attempts in 36 minutes.
 Despite the first three losses, Lendeborg is playing well, averaging 18.7 points, 8.3 rebounds, and 4.3 assists.
